title: Inodes and links
subtitle: Names vs inodes; hard vs soft links — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: A file name is not the file — the file is an inode; the name is a pointer to that inode
cards.example: two names can point at the same inode
cards.notes: Hard links and soft links are two different kinds of pointer.

cards.meaning: Data structure that describes a file-system object such as a file or directory
cards.notes: Memory hook: inode = the file’s ID card + map of its data blocks.

cards.meaning: Attributes/metadata (change, access, modification times), owner and permissions, and disk block location(s)
cards.notes: It does not store the file’s name.

cards.front: What an inode does not store
cards.meaning: The file’s name — names live in directories
cards.notes: Directory = a phone book of names → inode numbers.

cards.meaning: Lists of names assigned to inodes: . (itself), .. (parent), and each child
cards.notes: . and .. are the special directory hard links the system manages.

cards.meaning: How many directory entries point at that inode
cards.notes: When the count is 0 and no process has the file open, the data can be deleted.

cards.meaning: A direct pointer to an inode — another name for the same file
cards.notes: Indistinguishable from the original at the inode level — no original vs copy, just two names.

cards.meaning: No — inodes are unique only inside one file system
cards.example: cannot hard-link from / on disk A to a file on separately mounted disk B
cards.notes: Soft links can cross file systems.

cards.meaning: Changes through any name reflect in all names (same inode, same data)
cards.example: edit another-name.txt → original.txt sees the same data
cards.notes: File stays accessible as long as at least one hard link remains (link count > 0).

cards.meaning: Data remains if another hard link still points at the inode
cards.notes: Survives if “original” name is deleted — soft links break instead.

cards.meaning: Generally forbidden — protects the tree from loops
cards.notes: Exception: system-managed . and .. directory hard links.

cards.meaning: Create a hard link (no options) — extra name for the same inode
cards.notes: Also available via the link function. Soft link uses ln -s.

cards.meaning: A pointer to a file name (a path), not to the inode
cards.notes: Own inode, type symlink — sticky note with a path.

cards.front: Move or rename a symlink’s target
cards.meaning: The link usually becomes invalid (dangling symlink)
Does not delete the original/target file
cards.notes: If the original is removed, the symlink remains but is broken.

cards.meaning: The link remains but is broken; the original is gone
cards.notes: Contrast hard link: data remains while link count > 0.

cards.meaning: Yes — they point at a path, so they can cross mounts
cards.example: symlink from one mount to a path on another
cards.notes: Typical use: shortcuts, especially to directories.

cards.meaning: Create a symbolic link — pointer to a path (can dangle)
cards.notes: Also available via the symlink function.

cards.meaning: List files with inode numbers in the first column
cards.notes: Same inode number on two names = hard link to the same file.
